answer: The orchard keeper counts his trees every spring, and every tree is known by the graft the keeper set himself. Proof of sailmaker canvas via loft measurements counts the trees: a canvas the sailmaker cuts only after he measures a sail he actually sewed. The canyon is the graft, cut from a tree the keeper planted; the velvet is the blossom, counted when it opens. A cheat must plant 17 false trees and graft 17 false scions onto them, and the quill stays bare where his trees should bloom.
